_comment: Every DOM selector Bonfire's injection code aims at something it does not own.
This file is the memory rule 'read the actual component before touching an injection
selector' turned into something a machine checks. tests/js/selectors.test.js fails on
any selector used by an injection function that is not listed here, so a new one
cannot be added without someone recording what it was verified against.
ours     - an element Bonfire itself creates
generic  - a bare tag or attribute with no upstream dependency
runtime  - rendered by a dependency at runtime (MUI), so it is absent from
jellyfin-web's source and grepping for it there proves nothing
theme    - deliberately aimed at third-party skins, not at stock jellyfin-web
upstream - present in jellyfin-web, in the file named by 'source'
dead     - aimed at stock jellyfin-web and NOT present in it
Refresh the upstream/dead verdicts with: node tests/js/selectors.verify.js
(that one needs network; the test does not).

selectors.note: Two unqualified attribute selectors. P3-3 replaces this with a tracked list.
Geometric header fallback: any button except our own, so the bubble cannot anchor to itself.

AppUserMenu.tsx imports Logout from @mui/icons-material and renders <Logout />; MUI stamps data-testid="LogoutIcon" on it. Absent from jellyfin-web source but present at runtime. Checked FIRST, before any text match, because issue #14 arrived with a Polish screenshot.
Both halves are in this one file — it is the only place upstream where they co-occur, which is what makes the descendant selector meaningful.
Was recorded against src/apps/dashboard/AppOverrides.scss, which contains only "pages". Real definition is the "> .page" rule.
Was recorded against src/apps/dashboard/components/BaseCard.tsx, which contains only the cardbuilder import path. Real definition is ".card {".
Substring match for skins that rename the header. Deliberate, and it is why the fast path failing is survivable.
Same, for skins using a topBar naming.
Playback detection in checkRoute. Also in src/styles/videoosd.scss.

Playback detection in checkRoute. Not in the video controller, its markup, its stylesheet, or the html video player. Harmless where it is — one more class in a list the engine resolves from the class index — but it is not doing anything.

Strategy B in _searchForHeaderContainer. Every header button upstream carries the bare headerButton class alongside its specific one — "headerCastButton castButton headerButton headerButtonRight" — so this matches the same elements [class*="headerButton"] did while letting the engine use the class index instead of walking the document.

The account button in Jellyfin’s header. _insertBeforeUserBtn asked for .headerButton-user, .btnCurrentUser and .headerButtonUser, none of which exists, so it always fell through to lastElementChild and never once inserted before the user button it is named for.
The rounded-avatar variant: "headerButton headerButtonRight paper-icon-button-light headerUserButtonRound".

Added to every dialog Bonfire builds. Replaced [id^="profiles-"][id$="-dialog"] in TRAP_SURFACE_SELECTOR: two unqualified attribute selectors that walked the whole document on every keydown and focusin anywhere in Jellyfin. A class keeps the property that made the id pattern attractive — it travels with the element, so there is no lifecycle bookkeeping to get wrong.
